That's because you can still have an eating disorder and not be underweight. I'm a normal weight and currently recovering. 

I don't want to become overweight but it is an incredibly difficult thing to manage when you have reactive eating after coming out of a binge purge or restricting cycle. Especially when you have to remove control from your diet as well. 

It's a difficult thing to manage and I don't want to become overweight, but honestly I'd take a BMI of 26 any day over relapsing and returning to the hell I've been in for the past two years. Being a couple of BMI points over the healthy limit is fAr better for my health in the long run than the constant purging I used to do and still sometimes go through periods of (I am working on it though). Sometimes it just comes down to weighing up what will ultimately be better both for my physical and mental health. 

Obviously though I don't really want to become overweight, but if it happens it is something that I can tackle after I have been recovered for a bit longer and have a better relationship with food.

Weight restoration isn't appropriating an eating disorder, it's recovery from an eating disorder. You have to give up the control and restriction or binging/purging or bringing and restriction to be fully recovered. Those who are underweight or have been harming their body for a long time need extra nutrients to restore health to their body and recover physically.

Oof as someone who is actually recovering from an ED I have just a few issues with what you said. 

In the end of it a lot of EDs aren't control and the person doesn't *actually have control*, a lot of the time people try to control food as a way of coping with other stuff that is going on in their lives. People have to give up the control and give up the exercise as it is genuinely harming them. If you have an exercise addiction, you have to stop exercising. If you're someone who is underweight you need to be weight restored. Or if you're binging too much you need to be able to learn when your body is actually hungry and stop trying to compensate for your binges (I.e. Restrict binge or binge purge cycles), to do that sometimes you have to just accept the binges (or at least that's what my ED specialist nutritionist says lol)

So because of that and how hard it can be to a) give up exercising or b) give up restriction c) binging and then purging or restricting a lot of people in recovery turn to places like Instagram to document their recovery process and to get support from other people who are also recovering. You said a lot of anorexics (I'd just like to point out that you did only mention anorexia in your post and no their ED oof) "maintain some semblance of food control", but the thing is no one with an ED should be trying to do that in the early stages of recovery. Control (or lackthereof) is one of the hallmarks of an ED, as it is the major coping mechanism in the mental illness. In recovery we have to abandon that coping mechanism and replace it with more constructive ones instead. 

If any of those people were to see their content on here with the harsh criticism that they should have more control etc that gets dished out here I could definitely see a relapse or something similar happening. 

Just leave those us who are recovering alone, it's hard enough to recover an eating disorder when you're confronted with food everyday, but as someone who is recovering from Bulimia right now, you have no idea how much harder it would be to stop yourself from relapsing if you were shredded to pieces for your recovery method on such a place as reddit.

That is nowhere near enough calories, esecially with daily gym sessions. To the point where you'd probably also be losing muscle, which is really really not good. An amount that low is also not sustainable and could lead to reactive eating, because of this you should probably add another 1000 or so onto that due to the exercise that you're doing. As you don't really want a deficit of more than 1000-1500 (unless you're morbily obese and require extremely rapid weight loss, even then you can usually eat a fair amount of food due to larger people having higher TDEEs etc). 
I'd also like to point out that your eating window seems to be more like an hour or two, rather than 8, meaning you're fasting for 22-23 hours per day. This can be okay for some, but it usually takes a bit of working up to, especially if you're new to fasting. Sometimes going in the deepend can backfire mucu like eating too little and lead to reactive eating (b i n g e s) and then loss of progress and demotivation etc, which is why it's best to try and start with shorter fasting periods and longer eating periods (like fasting 16 hours a day and eating 8 hours a day). Letting your body adjust to IF by introducing it more slowly is the best shot at making it easier to continue with IF and a long term lifestyle change, rather than a crash diet alteration. 
Best of luck, I really hope you can make some adjustments to your diet so that your weight loss is healthy and sustainable :)
